module: "Pan" camera shared by the editor's spline tools. It takes over the editor's free camera (via toolCamera), switches to a top-down view and allows moving with right-click and zooming with the mouse wheel. A host tool registers it with configure, calls it every frame with drive, and can have it frame the current selection.
usage:
local pan = extensions.editor_toolUtilities_panCamera
pan.configure({focusProvider = function() return selectedPoints end})
pan.toggle()
-- every frame of the tool:
pan.drive(isDraggingNode)
notes: The state (on, focusProvider) is local to the module: only one pan camera at a time.
gotoPoints returns false if neither the pan camera nor toolCamera is active: the caller must then do its own free-camera jump.
Framing goes through util.splineFocus then toolCamera.flyPan; the altitude is relative to the terrain.

configure.desc: Registers a callback supplying the points of the current selection, used to frame them when the camera opens.

opts.desc: Table with the focusProvider field: function with no argument returning a list of {x,y,z} points or nil.

isOn.desc: Tells whether the pan camera is active.

returns.desc: true if the pan camera drives the view.

open.desc: Activates the pan camera (toolCamera.takeOver) and switches to top-down view: frames the selection supplied by focusProvider if there is one, otherwise switches to top-down view at the camera's current position and height.

close.desc: Deactivates the pan camera and hands the free camera back to the editor (toolCamera.handBack).

toggle.desc: Toggle: closes the pan camera if it is active, otherwise opens it.

gotoPoints.desc: "Go to" routing: if the pan camera (or toolCamera) is active, makes it fly to the given points and returns true; otherwise returns false and the caller does its normal jump.

returns.desc: true if the request was handled by the pan camera.

drive.desc: To be called every frame: applies movement (right-click drag) and zoom (mouse wheel) via toolCamera.drive.

blocked.desc: true to suspend movement during the tool's modal interactions (polygon drawing, node dragging, placement...).
